description: Adversarial missing fact test: In June 2027, a personal data breach is detected and noticed, but the exact timestamp when the entity became aware of the breach is unknown. The engine must emit an Unknown asking for awareness time.

incident_facts.description: Customer database breach observed in server logs.

unknowns.question: When did the entity become aware of the personal data breach?

labels_source: DPDP Rules 2025 Gazette GSR 846(E) page 26 Rule 7(2)(b)

source_quotes.quote:
(ii) Any service provider, intermediary, data centre, body corporate and 
Government organisation shall mandatorily report cyber incidents as 
mentioned in Annexure I to CERT-In within 6 hours of noticing such 
incidents or being brought to notice about such incidents. The incidents can 
be reported to CERT-In via email (incident@cert-in.org.in), Phone (1800-
11-4949) and Fax (1800-11-6969). The details regarding methods and 
formats of reporting cyber security incidents is also published on the 
website of CERT-In www.cert-in.org.in and will be updated from time to 
time.

(b) within seventy-two hours of becoming aware of the breach, or within such longer period as the 
Board may allow on a request made in writing in this behalf, —
